## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. **The planned pilot will focus on a single, clear target metric: gathering feedback on user satisfaction scored on a 1-5 scale.** A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance).

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, and design of a human-centered interface.

## Risks & Challenges
Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. **A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.**
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. **A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools.**
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance). **A proposed, limited-time, small-scale beta program for the Enterprise Programs is planned, targeting a single department (e.g., marketing) within a proposed partner company to gather feedback.**

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, and design of a human-centered interface.

Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## One-Sentence Summary

An online learning platform focused on human-centered AI education is evolving into an interactive, creator-driven ecosystem with a personal AI mentor, a hands-on agent playground, and tools for educators to publish micro-courses.

## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking. **A proposed, limited-scope pilot for the AI Agent Playground with a defined user group (e.g., 25 small business owners) is planned to test the 'invoice assistance' template and gather feedback on usability before the 2026 launch.**
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance).

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, and design of a human-centered interface.

## Risks & Challenges
Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## One-Sentence Summary

An online learning platform focused on human-centered AI education is evolving into an interactive, creator-driven ecosystem with a personal AI mentor, a hands-on agent playground, and tools for educators to publish micro-courses.

## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. A proposed, small-scale user research initiative is planned before prototype development to gather input on desired mentor personality and communication style from 30 potential users across beginner and intermediate segments. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy, comparing two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measuring success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance).
- **Proposed Onboarding Optimization:** A proposed, specific A/B test for the platform's onboarding flow for individual learners is planned. This test would compare two different content recommendation approaches (e.g., a skill-based assessment versus an interest-based selection) and measure a specific metric like 'time to first completed lesson'.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback and a proposed user research initiative on mentor personality, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, design of a human-centered interface, and proposed user research initiatives, including the proposed onboarding A/B test.

## Risks & Challenges
Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## One-Sentence Summary

An online learning platform focused on human-centered AI education is evolving into an interactive, creator-driven ecosystem with a personal AI mentor, a hands-on agent playground, and tools for educators to publish micro-courses.

## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. A proposed, small-scale user research initiative is planned before prototype development to gather input on desired mentor personality and communication style from 30 potential users across beginner and intermediate segments. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking. A proposed, small-scale pilot test of the Agent Playground with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers) is planned to gather initial feedback on template usability before the 2026 launch.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance). A proposed, small-scale user research initiative with 20-30 potential enterprise clients is planned to gather input on desired features for the 'Enterprise Programs' before development.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback and a proposed user research initiative on mentor personality, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), preceded by a proposed pilot test on template usability, (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026). The proposed user research initiative for Enterprise Programs would be conducted prior to the development of these features.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, design of a human-centered interface, and proposed user research and pilot test initiatives, including the proposed research with enterprise clients.

## Risks & Challenges
Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. A proposed, small-scale user research initiative is planned before prototype development to gather input on desired mentor personality and communication style from 30 potential users across beginner and intermediate segments. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking. A proposed, small-scale pilot test of the Agent Playground with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers) is planned to gather initial feedback on template usability before the 2026 launch.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance). A proposed, small-scale user research initiative with 20-30 potential enterprise clients is planned to gather input on desired features for the 'Enterprise Programs' before development.
- **Onboarding Optimization:** A proposed, specific A/B test for the platform's onboarding flow for new individual learners is planned. This test would compare two different introductory paths and measure a specific metric like 'time to first completed micro-lesson'.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback and a proposed user research initiative on mentor personality, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), preceded by a proposed pilot test on template usability, (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026). The proposed user research initiative for Enterprise Programs would be conducted prior to the development of these features. The proposed A/B test for the new learner onboarding flow would be integrated into the platform's ongoing optimization efforts.

Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, design of a human-centered interface, and proposed user research and pilot test initiatives, including the proposed research with enterprise clients and the proposed A/B test for learner onboarding.

## Risks & Challenges
Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance). Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. A proposed, small-scale user research initiative is planned before prototype development to gather input on desired mentor personality and communication style from 30 potential users across beginner and intermediate segments. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking. A proposed, small-scale pilot test of the Agent Playground with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers) is planned to gather initial feedback on template usability before the 2026 launch.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'. A proposed, specific A/B test comparing two different pricing structures for creator monetization tools is also planned to gather feedback on optimal pricing models.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance). A proposed, small-scale user research initiative with 20-30 potential enterprise clients is planned to gather input on desired features for the 'Enterprise Programs' before development.
- **Onboarding Optimization:** A proposed, specific A/B test for the platform's onboarding flow for new individual learners is planned. This test would compare two different introductory paths and measure a specific metric like 'time to first completed micro-lesson'.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## One-Sentence Summary

An online learning platform focused on human-centered AI education is evolving into an interactive, creator-driven ecosystem with a personal AI mentor, a hands-on agent playground, and tools for educators to publish micro-courses.

## Problem
The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview
The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills. A proposed, small-scale user research initiative is planned before prototype development to gather input on desired mentor personality and communication style from 30 potential users across beginner and intermediate segments. The team plans a small-scale pilot test of the AI Mentor with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers from the existing learner base) to gather initial feedback before the 2026 prototype. A proposed, specific A/B test for the AI Mentor's recommendation algorithm is planned to gather targeted feedback on personalization efficacy. This test would compare two distinct user segments, such as beginners versus intermediate learners, and measure success using a specific, proposed metric: the comparison of lesson completion rates between the two segments.
- **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking. A proposed, small-scale pilot test of the Agent Playground with a defined user group (e.g., 50 beta testers) is planned to gather initial feedback on template usability before the 2026 launch.
- **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven. A planned, limited-time partnership with one or two established creator-educators in the AI space is proposed to co-develop and promote a flagship micro-course using the new Course Builder tools. A proposed, specific A/B test for the Course Builder tools is also planned, comparing two different onboarding flows for creator-educators and measuring a specific metric like 'time to publish first micro-lesson'.
- **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage. A proposed, specific A/B test for the 'Learning Content & Certifications' presentation format is planned, comparing two different UI layouts for micro-lessons and measuring a specific metric like 'scroll depth' or 'click-through to next lesson'.
- **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance). A proposed, small-scale user research initiative with 20-30 potential enterprise clients is planned to gather input on desired features for the 'Enterprise Programs' before development. A proposed, small-scale pilot test of the enterprise programs with 2-3 identified partner organizations is planned before full development.
- **Onboarding Optimization:** A proposed, specific A/B test for the platform's onboarding flow for new individual learners is planned. This test would compare two different introductory paths and measure a specific metric like 'time to first completed micro-lesson'.
- **Global Challenge Pilot:** A proposed, small-scale pilot of the 'Global Challenge' concept is planned as a time-bound, online event for the existing community. This pilot would test engagement mechanics and gather feedback on potential reward structures before the full launch.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status
The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), preceded by a planned pilot test with a small user group for feedback and a proposed user research initiative on mentor personality, (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), preceded by a proposed pilot test on template usability, (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026). The proposed user research initiative for Enterprise Programs and the proposed small-scale pilot test with 2-3 partner organizations would be conducted prior to the development of these features. The proposed A/B test for the new learner onboarding flow would be integrated into the platform's ongoing optimization efforts. The proposed small-scale pilot of the Global Challenge concept would be conducted to inform the full launch.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, design of a human-centered interface, and proposed user research and pilot test initiatives, including the proposed research with enterprise clients, the proposed pilot test with partner organizations, the proposed A/B test for learner onboarding, the proposed Global Challenge pilot, and the proposed A/B test for the learning content presentation format.

## Risks & Challenges
Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships
The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included
Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details
Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that helps basketball players discover nearby games, check in at courts, and build verified rankings and leaderboards to motivate play and community connection.

## Problem

The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview

The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.

-   Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.

-   Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression.

-   Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).

-   A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

## Development Status

According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025, followed by growth to tens of thousands of downloads and several thousand active users in early 2026.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned milestones include:

-   A phased beta beginning November 2025, emphasizing feedback-driven fixes.

-   Marketing pushes via social channels and in-person pop-up events.

-   Post-beta growth goals into early 2026.

-   A potential later phase unlocking AI stat insights after initial targets are met.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds are intended to: strengthen real-time mapping and ranking capabilities on a no-code platform; run targeted social-media advertising to drive initial downloads; and host regional pop-up events for hands-on testing and family-focused engagement.

## Risks & Challenges

Acknowledged risks include: technical bugs in the no-code stack during beta (mitigated by phased testing and feedback loops); difficulty gaining adoption in a crowded sports-tech space (addressed through targeted ads and local events); potential delays in fulfilling non-digital perks (addressed via on-demand production partners and sequencing digital items first); and founder bandwidth constraints (managed by strict milestone prioritization and openness to adding help).

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by the founders as a lean, solo-driven initiative leveraging no-code development. The page references outreach to recognizable sports-media partners and print-on-demand suppliers to amplify awareness and streamline merchandise fulfillment.

## What's Included

Access to the app's core experience: real-time court maps, player check-ins, and verified rankings/leaderboards as described for launch.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The creators emphasize iterative development, with phased testing, user feedback loops, and ongoing updates after launch to improve reliability and expand features.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that helps basketball players discover nearby games, check in at courts, and build verified rankings and leaderboards to motivate play and community connection.

## Problem
The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview
The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.
- Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.
- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

## Development Status & Beta Testing Hypothesis
According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. To validate core engagement and local network density, we plan to test specific hypotheses with the first 100 beta users: we hypothesize that 70% of beta testers will check in at a court at least twice a week. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include:
- A phased beta beginning November 2025, emphasizing feedback-driven fixes and testing the engagement and network-density hypotheses.
- Marketing pushes via social channels and in-person pop-up events.
- Post-beta growth goals into early 2026.
- A potential later phase unlocking AI stat insights after initial targets are met.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds are intended to: strengthen real-time mapping and ranking capabilities on a no-code platform; run targeted social-media advertising to drive initial downloads; and host regional pop-up events for hands-on testing and family-focused engagement.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include: technical bugs in the no-code stack during beta (mitigated by phased testing and feedback loops); difficulty gaining adoption in a crowded sports-tech space (addressed through targeted ads and local events); potential delays in fulfilling non-digital perks (addressed via on-demand production partners and sequencing digital items first); and founder bandwidth constraints (managed by strict milestone prioritization and openness to adding help).

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by the founders as a lean, solo-driven initiative leveraging no-code development. The page references outreach to recognizable sports-media partners and print-on-demand suppliers to amplify awareness and streamline merchandise fulfillment.

## What's Included
Access to the app's core experience: real-time court maps, player check-ins, and verified rankings/leaderboards as described for launch.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The creators emphasize iterative development, with phased testing, user feedback loops, and ongoing updates after launch to improve reliability and expand features.

A mobile app that helps basketball players discover nearby games, check in at courts, and build verified rankings and leaderboards to motivate play and community connection.

## Problem
The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview
The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.
- Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.
- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

## Development Status & Beta Testing Hypothesis
According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. To validate core engagement and local network density, we plan to test specific hypotheses with the first 100 beta users: we hypothesize that 70% of beta testers will check in at a court at least twice a week. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location, with a target of under 5 miles to demonstrate hyper-local density.

To further test engagement drivers, we propose incorporating a simple gamification element during the beta phase, such as a 'Court Streak' badge awarded for consecutive weekly check-ins, to measure its effect on the core engagement hypothesis.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include:
- A phased beta beginning November 2025, emphasizing feedback-driven fixes and testing the engagement and network-density hypotheses, including the proposed gamification test.
- Marketing pushes via social channels and in-person pop-up events.
- Post-beta growth goals into early 2026.
- A potential later phase unlocking AI stat insights after initial targets are met.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds are intended to: strengthen real-time mapping and ranking capabilities on a no-code platform; run targeted social-media advertising to drive initial downloads; and host regional pop-up events for hands-on testing and family-focused engagement.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include: technical bugs in the no-code stack during beta (mitigated by phased testing and feedback loops); difficulty gaining adoption in a crowded sports-tech space (addressed through targeted ads and local events); potential delays in fulfilling non-digital perks (addressed via on-demand production partners and sequencing digital items first); and founder bandwidth constraints (managed by strict milestone prioritization and openness to adding help).

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by the founders as a lean, solo-driven initiative leveraging no-code development. The page references outreach to recognizable sports-media partners and print-on-demand suppliers to amplify awareness and streamline merchandise fulfillment.

## What's Included
Access to the app's core experience: real-time court maps, player check-ins, and verified rankings/leaderboards as described for launch.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The creators emphasize iterative development, with phased testing, user feedback loops, and ongoing updates after launch to improve reliability and expand features.

## One-Sentence Summary
A mobile app that helps basketball players discover nearby games, check in at courts, and build verified rankings and leaderboards to motivate play and community connection.

## Problem
The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview
The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.
- Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.
- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression. To ensure integrity, a lightweight verification method is proposed for the beta test, such as requiring a second user present at the game to confirm a result before it updates the leaderboards.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

## Development Status & Beta Testing Hypothesis
According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. To validate core engagement and local network density, we plan to test specific hypotheses with the first 100 beta users: we hypothesize that 70% of beta testers will check in at a court at least twice a week. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location, with a target of under 5 miles to demonstrate hyper-local density.

To further test engagement drivers, we propose incorporating a simple gamification element during the beta phase, such as a 'Court Streak' badge awarded for consecutive weekly check-ins, to measure its effect on the core engagement hypothesis. The proposed lightweight verification method for rankings will also be tested as part of the beta to assess its feasibility and user acceptance.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include:
- A phased beta beginning November 2025, emphasizing feedback-driven fixes and testing the engagement and network-density hypotheses, including the proposed gamification test and the verification method for rankings.
- Marketing pushes via social channels and in-person pop-up events.
- Post-beta growth goals into early 2026.
- A potential later phase unlocking AI stat insights after initial targets are met.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds are intended to: strengthen real-time mapping and ranking capabilities on a no-code platform; run targeted social-media advertising to drive initial downloads; and host regional pop-up events for hands-on testing and family-focused engagement.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include: technical bugs in the no-code stack during beta (mitigated by phased testing and feedback loops); difficulty gaining adoption in a crowded sports-tech space (addressed through targeted ads and local events); potential delays in fulfilling non-digital perks (addressed via on-demand production partners and sequencing digital items first); and founder bandwidth constraints (managed by strict milestone prioritization and openness to adding help). The proposed verification method may introduce friction; this will be monitored during beta testing.

The effort is led by the founders as a lean, solo-driven initiative leveraging no-code development. The page references outreach to recognizable sports-media partners and print-on-demand suppliers to amplify awareness and streamline merchandise fulfillment.

## What's Included
Access to the app's core experience: real-time court maps, player check-ins, and verified rankings/leaderboards as described for launch.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The creators emphasize iterative development, with phased testing, user feedback loops, and ongoing updates after launch to improve reliability and expand features.

## One-Sentence Summary
A mobile app that helps basketball players discover nearby games, check in at courts, and build verified rankings and leaderboards to motivate play and community connection.

## Problem
The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview
The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.
- Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.
- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression. To ensure integrity, a lightweight verification method is proposed for the beta test, such as requiring a second user present at the game to confirm a result before it updates the leaderboards.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

## Development Status & Beta Testing Hypothesis
According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. To validate core engagement and local network density, we plan to test specific hypotheses with the first 100 beta users: we hypothesize that 70% of beta testers will check in at a court at least twice a week. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location, with a target of under 5 miles to demonstrate hyper-local density.

To further test engagement drivers, we propose incorporating a simple gamification element during the beta phase, such as a 'Court Streak' badge awarded for consecutive weekly check-ins, to measure its effect on the core engagement hypothesis. The proposed lightweight verification method for rankings will also be tested as part of the beta to assess its feasibility and user acceptance.

To enhance local network density during the beta phase, we propose seeking a partnership with a national chain of community centers or a well-known youth basketball organization to pilot the app in their facilities. This would be framed as a potential future collaboration to be explored and tested.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include:
- A phased beta beginning November 2025, emphasizing feedback-driven fixes and testing the engagement and network-density hypotheses, including the proposed gamification test, the verification method for rankings, and the potential partnership pilot.
- Marketing pushes via social channels and in-person pop-up events.
- Post-beta growth goals into early 2026.
- A potential later phase unlocking AI stat insights after initial targets are met.

The effort is led by the founders as a lean, solo-driven initiative leveraging no-code development. A partnership with a national chain of community centers or a well-known youth basketball organization is proposed to be explored for a potential pilot during the beta phase.

Access to the app's core experience: real-time court maps, player check-ins, and verified rankings/leaderboards as described for launch.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The creators emphasize iterative development, with phased testing, user feedback loops, and ongoing updates after launch to improve reliability and expand features.

The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. - Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.

- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression. To ensure integrity, a lightweight verification method is proposed for the beta test, such as requiring a second user present at the game to confirm a result before it updates the leaderboards.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. To validate core engagement and local network density, we plan to test specific hypotheses with the first 100 beta users: we hypothesize that 70% of beta testers will check in at a court at least twice a week. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location, with a target of under 5 miles to demonstrate hyper-local density.

To further test engagement drivers, we propose incorporating a simple gamification element during the beta phase, such as a 'Court Streak' badge awarded for consecutive weekly check-ins. To quantitatively demonstrate its motivational impact, we propose testing a specific target: aiming for a 20% increase in weekly check-ins among users who earn the badge. A mobile app that helps basketball players discover nearby games, check in at courts, and build verified rankings and leaderboards to motivate play and community connection.

## Problem
The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview
The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.
- Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.
- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression. To ensure integrity, a lightweight verification method is proposed for the beta test, such as requiring a second user present at the game to confirm a result before it updates the leaderboards.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A proposed, simple feature for the beta test: a 'Game Creator' button that lets a user declare an intent to play at a specific court and time.
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.
- A proposed, simple revenue model for future consideration: a freemium tier where verified rankings and advanced leaderboard analytics could become part of a low-cost monthly subscription. This is explicitly framed as a potential post-beta monetization path to be validated.

The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. To validate core engagement and local network density, we plan to test specific hypotheses with the first 100 beta users: we hypothesize that 70% of beta testers will check in at a court at least twice a week. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location, with a target of under 5 miles to demonstrate hyper-local density.

To further test engagement drivers, we propose incorporating a simple gamification element during the beta phase, such as a 'Court Streak' badge awarded for consecutive weekly check-ins. To quantitatively demonstrate its motivational impact, we propose testing a specific target: aiming for a 20% increase in weekly check-ins among users who earn the badge. The proposed lightweight verification method for rankings will also be tested as part of the beta to assess its feasibility and user acceptance.

We also propose to test the new 'Game Creator' feature during the beta. A specific target metric to measure its effectiveness is proposed: tracking how many declared games result in at least one other user checking in.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include:
- A phased beta beginning November 2025, emphasizing feedback-driven fixes and testing the engagement and network-density hypotheses, including the proposed gamification test (with its 20% increase target), the verification method for rankings, and the proposed test of the 'Game Creator' feature and its target metric.
- Marketing pushes via social channels and in-person pop-up events.
- Post-beta growth goals into early 2026.
- A potential later phase unlocking AI stat insights after initial targets are met.
- The proposed freemium revenue model would be considered for validation and potential implementation only after the beta phase.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include: technical bugs in the no-code stack during beta (mitigated by phased testing and feedback loops); difficulty gaining adoption in a crowded sports-tech space (addressed through targeted ads and local events); potential delays in fulfilling non-digital perks (addressed via on-demand production partners and sequencing digital items first); and founder bandwidth constraints (managed by strict milestone prioritization and openness to adding help). The proposed verification method may introduce friction; this will be monitored during beta testing. The proposed freemium model, if pursued, carries the risk of user acceptance and must be validated.

The effort is led by the founders as a lean, solo-driven initiative leveraging no-code development. The page references outreach to recognizable sports-media partners and print-on-demand suppliers to amplify awareness and streamline merchandise fulfillment.

Access to the app's core experience: real-time court maps, player check-ins, and verified rankings/leaderboards as described for launch.

The creators emphasize iterative development, with phased testing, user feedback loops, and ongoing updates after launch to improve reliability and expand features. The proposed freemium model is a potential future consideration for post-beta validation.

## Problem
The creators describe a gap for everyday players---parents, kids, and recreational athletes---who struggle to find reliable, pickup-friendly games and a way to track progress beyond informal word-of-mouth. They frame this as both a logistics problem (knowing where and when people are playing) and a motivation problem (recognition, friendly competition, and belonging).

## Solution / Product Overview
The project proposes a mobile app that maps active courts in real time, enables player check-ins to signal activity, and maintains verified rankings so users can "climb" leaderboards. It aims to turn empty courts into active meetups and to give players a persistent identity anchored in participation and results.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- Real-time court mapping to show where games are happening.
- Player check-ins to validate court activity and attendance.
- Verified rankings and leaderboards to track progression. To ensure integrity, a lightweight verification method is proposed for the beta test, such as requiring a second user present at the game to confirm a result before it updates the leaderboards.
- Social elements for sharing moments and celebrating wins (as described).
- A proposed, simple feature for the beta test: a 'Game Creator' button that lets a user declare an intent to play at a specific court and time.
- A potential future enhancement: AI-driven stat insights, contingent on later development milestones.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The creators call out recreational players across ages, including parents returning to the game and kids discovering it. Primary scenarios include finding immediate games near home, signaling interest by checking in, and competing on leaderboards with local peers.

According to the page, a working prototype has been tested with roughly 50 local players. A teaser site and an AI demo video are mentioned. The roadmap cites a beta release targeted for November 2025. As a proposed metric to demonstrate local network density, we plan to track the average check-in distance from a user's home location, with a target of under 5 miles to demonstrate hyper-local density.
